diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU distance changed abruptly from 112 to 268 while remaining constant before and after the step. The RX power moved with that path change, from approximately -19.4 dBm to -22.1 dBm, so the optical change is a consequence of a changed fibre path or incorrect ONU/path record rather than progressive fibre degradation.
evidence: The live ONU is responding and online, with RX power -22.05 dBm and TX power 2.37 dBm, both within the calibrated normal ranges.
The customer's peers on EPON0/3 are online and responding, so there is no evidence of a shared PON, splitter, port, or OLT failure.
OLT ping, SNMP, metrics, and all six tested PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat and VLAN walk are also normal.
RX telemetry was stable around -19.4 dBm for most of the window, then stepped to approximately -22.1 dBm and remained there; this is not a gradual decline.

Distance was constant at 112 before the same timestamp and stepped to 268, remaining constant afterward. Distance is fixed geometry, so this step identifies a changed fibre path or incorrect path record.
TX power and TX bias current remained stable and healthy, providing no evidence of laser degradation.
The session count is three in 24 hours with approximately 658-minute average duration, so the customer is not flapping and there is no authentication-based fault.
The current optical level remains usable, therefore the primary fault is the path or record change, classified as distance_change rather than fiber_degradation.

remediation.action: Verify the physical fibre route, patching, splitter assignment, and ONU registration for EPON0/3:17. Check whether the customer was moved to a different path or whether the OLT/CRM record points to the wrong ONU. Restore the intended path or correct the inventory/provisioning record, then confirm that distance and RX power return to the expected values.

ground_truth.root_cause: The measured optical distance stepped from 112 m to 268 m two and a half days ago, with a matching 2.7 dB RX drop. The fibre path was physically re-routed, most likely a re-splice or a patch onto a different feeder.
expected_reasoning: RX dropped from -19.4 to -22.1 dBm, which alone would suggest attenuation
The drop is a single step, not a slope, and RX has been stable at the new level since
Distance stepped from 112 m to 268 m at the same moment
Distance is constant per customer in normal operation, so a step means the physical path changed
The 2.7 dB loss is consistent with 156 m of additional fibre plus a splice
TX power, bias current and supply voltage are all unchanged, so the ONU is not involved
RTT timing quantum of 96 corroborates the longer path
Service is unaffected: sessions and traffic are normal at the new signal level
This is a recorded path change, not a developing fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Confirm the re-route was intentional and update plant records

distractors: The RX drop looks like fibre degradation if distance is not consulted
The trigger is phrased as an RX threshold breach, pointing at the wrong signal
Service is unaffected, inviting a no_fault conclusion
